final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is substantively useful because it abandons the unsupported claim that rollout controls alone make the launch compliant. But the narrowed position still depends on a missing predicate: admissible evidence that the launch materials actually include explicit disclosure of the field-service dispatch limitation, or alternatively an approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. The available evidence still shows the exposed segment remains in scope, is below target on technician safety-note routing, and is not covered by a completed reviewed risk acceptance. Under the stated policy, those facts leave compliance unresolved. This is not enough for compliant_with_caveats, because the caveat is not merely descriptive; it is the very compliance condition that has not been evidenced as satisfied.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the final model card or launch packet actually discloses the field-service dispatch limitation before launch.
No approved risk acceptance specifically covers continued exposure of the field-service dispatch segment.
The affected field-service dispatch use case remains in the initial randomized rollout cohort despite being below target on technician safety-note routing.
Policy text says rollout controls, rollback capability, dashboards, or a small initial percentage do not remove disclosure duties while the affected segment remains exposed.
The Actor's narrowed position is conditional on future disclosure, but that condition is still an unresolved compliance predicate on this record.
